newsitem.title: USA: Artra Group sees higher Q1 earnings.
newsitem.headline: Artra Group sees higher Q1 earnings.

text.p: Artra Group Inc said Tuesday it expects earnings for the first quarter will exceed year-ago levels.
In the first quarter of 1996, Artra had an operating profit of $959,000 or $0.09 a share before a gain of $1.23 a share.
Artra said it also expects results for the remainder of 1997 will benefit from near-term stability of favorable raw material prices and its recently acquired AB Specialty Holding Co operations.

Artra also cited a projected surge in food service distribution sales related to retail fast-food burger discounting and promotional pricing, lower interest expenses, and continued operating efficiencies.

Earlier, Artra reported a fourth quarter loss from continuing operations of $0.04 a share, compared with a year-ago loss of $0.73. For the year, earnings from continuing operations were $0.28 a share, compared with a year-ago loss of $2.69.

Artra said its Bagcraft Corp of America packaging subsidiary produced its highest operating earnings since it was acquired in 1990. Artra said Bagcraft is expected to post another record-setting performance in 1997.
Contributing to Bagcraft's 1996 performance was an eight percent decrease in the cost of sales from continuing operations due to lower paper costs.
